knowledge-base.overview: React 18+ guardrails, component patterns, hooks rules, state management, routing, forms, and testing. Applies to TypeScript-first React SPAs using Vite, React Router v6, TanStack Query, Zustand, and React Hook Form. Loaded automatically when agents work on .tsx or .jsx files.

core-principles.principle: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state. Each component has a single, clear responsibility.
Describe what the UI should look like; React handles all DOM updates. Never manipulate the DOM directly.
Props flow down, callbacks flow up. Avoid reverse data flow or sibling-to-sibling communication without shared state.
Prefer component composition and custom hooks over class hierarchies. Never use class components in new code.
All components use TypeScript with strict prop interfaces. No implicit any in component files.

guardrail.rule: Use functional components exclusively. Class components are forbidden in new code.
Only call hooks at the top level. Never inside conditions, loops, or nested functions. Only call from React function components or custom hooks.
Always include all dependencies in useEffect, useMemo, and useCallback arrays. Missing deps cause stale-closure bugs. Use eslint-plugin-react-hooks to enforce this.
Every component must have a TypeScript interface for its props. Never use inline object types or `any` for props.
guardrail.bad: function Card({ title, children }: { title: string; children: any }) {}

guardrail.rule: Clean up side effects in useEffect return function. Subscriptions, timers, and event listeners must be removed on unmount.
Name custom hooks with the `use` prefix. This is required for the React hooks linter to recognize and validate them.
Use `React.ReactNode` for children props, not `JSX.Element`. ReactNode accepts strings, arrays, null — JSX.Element does not.
Keep components under 200 lines. If a component exceeds this, split it into smaller focused components or extract custom hooks.
Prefer `useReducer` over `useState` when state has multiple sub-fields or transitions depend on previous state.
Avoid prop drilling beyond 2 levels. Use component composition, Context API, or Zustand for deeper sharing.
Never store derived state in useState. Compute derived values during render or with useMemo.
guardrail.bad: const [fullName, setFullName] = useState(`${first} ${last}`); // derived — will go stale

guardrail.rule: Use `React.memo()` only for expensive pure components after measuring. Premature memoization adds overhead without benefit.
Lazy-load routes and heavy components with `React.lazy()` and `Suspense`. Keep initial bundle under 200 KB.
Use accessible attributes on interactive elements: ARIA roles, labels, and keyboard navigation. Every interactive element must be reachable by keyboard.
Co-locate component, styles, and tests in the same directory. Avoid a flat tests/ folder for component tests.

project-structure.example: my-app/ ├── public/ │ └── index.html ├── src/ │ ├── assets/ # Static assets (images, fonts) │ ├── components/ │ │ ├── ui/ # Base UI components (Button, Input, Modal) │ │ └── features/ # Feature-specific components │ ├── hooks/ # Shared custom hooks │ ├── contexts/ # React contexts (AuthContext, ThemeContext) │ ├── services/ # API services (fetch wrappers, API clients) │ ├── utils/ # Utility functions │ ├── types/ # TypeScript types │ ├── pages/ # Page components (route-level only) │ ├── App.tsx │ ├── main.tsx │ └── index.css ├── package.json ├── tsconfig.json ├── vite.config.ts └── README.md

notes.note: components/ui/ for reusable design system primitives
hooks/ for shared custom hooks; feature-specific hooks co-locate with component
pages/ for route-level components only — no business logic

pattern.name: Functional Component with Props
pattern.description: Standard functional component with typed props, loading state, and conditional rendering.

pattern.name: Component with Children
pattern.description: Wrapper/container component accepting ReactNode children and optional footer slot.

pattern.name: Context API (Auth, Theme, Locale)
pattern.description: Use Context for low-frequency global state. Always export a typed hook; throw if used outside provider.

pattern.name: TanStack Query (Server State)
pattern.description: Use TanStack Query for all data fetching and server cache management. Never store server data in useState.

pattern.name: Zustand (Complex Client State)
pattern.description: Use Zustand for complex cross-component client state. Keep stores small and focused by domain.

routing.description: React Router v6 with lazy-loaded routes and Suspense.

forms.description: React Hook Form + Zod for type-safe, validated forms. Derive form types from Zod schemas — single source of truth.

rules.rule: Use userEvent over fireEvent — userEvent simulates real browser interactions
Test behavior, not implementation details (no state inspection, no internal method calls)
Query by accessible roles and labels first; test IDs are last resort
Mock API calls (services layer), not internal component state
Coverage target: greater than 80% for business logic components

quick-reference.item: Functional only, PascalCase.tsx, under 200 lines, typed props interface
Top-level only, use prefix, all deps declared, cleanup in useEffect return
Context API with typed hook + provider guard
TanStack Query — never useState for fetched data
React Router v6 with lazy() + Suspense per route
React Testing Library + userEvent; test behavior not internals
Under 200 KB initial load; code-split aggressively with lazy()
Measure first; React.memo / useMemo / useCallback only when profiler shows benefit
